Sommaire du poste Relevant du gestionnaire principal, Optimisation de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et transformation numérique, l’analyste principal(e) agit à titre de propriétaire fonctionnel de la capacité d’optimisation des stocks au sein des Opérations d’approvisionnement. Le/la titulaire dirige des initiatives complexes d’optimisation et de transformation numérique, traduit les données en recommandations d’affaires concrètes et met en place des pratiques analytiques évolutives qui améliorent les niveaux de stock, le service, les coûts, l’efficacité opérationnelle et la prise de décision. Le rôle combine une expertise approfondie en gestion des stocks avec des compétences avancées en analytique, en transformation numérique, en gouvernance des données et en amélioration continue. L’analyste est responsable de la conception et de l’évolution des méthodologies d’optimisation des stocks, des stratégies de réapprovisionnement, des paramètres de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des technologies de soutien et des capacités d’aide à la décision. Il/elle assure également la traduction de la Politique de gestion des stocks approuvée en méthodologies d’optimisation, paramètres, contrôles et recommandations, en partenariat avec le propriétaire de la politique et les équipes opérationnelles. Agissant comme un pont entre les équipes de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et les partenaires en données, analytique, intelligence artificielle et technologie, l’analyste relie les défis d’affaires à des solutions pratiques, évolutives et durables qui demeurent pertinentes sur le plan opérationnel, bien gouvernées, intégrées aux processus et adoptées par les utilisateurs. Le succès dans ce rôle repose sur une solide compréhension de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et des enjeux d’affaires, une curiosité à comprendre le fonctionnement des équipes opérationnelles ainsi que la capacité d’appliquer les données, l’analytique, l’automatisation et les technologies émergentes afin de générer une valeur d’affaires mesurable. Section A - Responsabilités spécifiques Stratégie et optimisation des stocks, 25% Être responsable de l’évolution des méthodologies d’optimisation des stocks, des stratégies de réapprovisionnement et des paramètres de la chaîne d’approvisionnement afin de soutenir les objectifs de niveau de service, de stocks, financiers et opérationnels. Diriger l’évaluation, l’optimisation, la surveillance, la gouvernance et la validation des paramètres de stocks et de réapprovisionnement dans Blue Yonder/JDA. Concevoir et réaliser des analyses avancées, des simulations, des modélisations de scénarios et des tests d’hypothèses afin d’identifier des occasions d’optimisation, de remettre en question les hypothèses en place, d’évaluer différentes options et de recommander des améliorations durables et évolutives. Définir et suivre les indicateurs de performance liés aux stocks, établir des liens entre les résultats et les objectifs stratégiques, et identifier de façon proactive les risques, les causes fondamentales ainsi que les mesures correctives et préventives requises. Traduire les résultats des modèles et les constats analytiques en recommandations concrètes permettant d’équilibrer les niveaux de stocks, les jours de stock disponibles (JDS), les niveaux de service, les coûts et les contraintes opérationnelles. Présenter les options, les compromis, les analyses de rentabilisation, les bénéfices attendus et les risques afin d’influencer les décisions de la direction et les priorités d’investissement. Solutions numériques et analytique (25 %) Diriger la conception, la maintenance, l’amélioration et la gouvernance des outils analytiques, tableaux de bord, modèles d’optimisation et solutions d’aide à la décision utilisés par les Opérations d’approvisionnement. Développer des capacités flexibles et évolutives pouvant s’adapter aux besoins d’affaires, aux priorités et aux modèles opérationnels en constante évolution. Piloter la modernisation des capacités analytiques grâce à l’automatisation, à la standardisation, à l’intégration de capacités basées sur l’intelligence artificielle et à l’arrimage avec les plateformes de données d’entreprise. Agir comme intermédiaire entre les équipes de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et les partenaires en données, analytique, intelligence artificielle et technologie afin de traduire les besoins d’affaires en exigences et en solutions évolutives. Identifier et diriger les occasions de simplifier les processus, de réduire les efforts manuels et d’améliorer la qualité des décisions ainsi que les résultats d’affaires en tirant parti des technologies analytiques, d’automatisation, d’intelligence artificielle et de transformation numérique les plus appropriées. Gestion des données, intelligence d’affaires et gouvernance, 20% Diriger des activités complexes d’extraction, de transformation, d’intégration, de validation et de résolution de problèmes liés aux données à travers les systèmes opérationnels et corporatifs, afin d’assurer la fiabilité et l’utilisabilité des données. Définir et assurer la gouvernance des ensembles de données, des intégrations, des règles d’affaires, des définitions de données et de la documentation soutenant les analyses de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et les solutions numériques. Promouvoir une saine gestion des données en améliorant leur qualité, leur intégrité, leur accessibilité, leur transparence et leur compréhension par les utilisateurs d’affaires. Établir et maintenir des standards analytiques, des pratiques de gouvernance des données, des méthodologies de validation et des cadres de production de rapports afin de soutenir une prise de décision cohérente et fondée sur les données. Encadrer et réviser le travail des analystes, lorsque requis, afin d’assurer le respect des standards établis en matière de données, de production de rapports et de gouvernance. Projets stratégiques et amélioration continue, 25% Diriger des initiatives stratégiques liées à l’optimisation des stocks, à l’intelligence d’affaires, à la modernisation des capacités analytiques, à l’automatisation, à la transformation numérique évolutive et à l’amélioration des processus. Collaborer avec des partenaires interfonctionnels afin d’identifier des opportunités, d’analyser les causes fondamentales et les solutions de rechange, d’aligner les priorités et de mettre en œuvre des solutions d’affaires durables. Réaliser des analyses ponctuelles complexes, élaborer des recommandations et construire des analyses de rentabilisation afin de soutenir les objectifs du service et de l’organisation. Job Summary Reporting to the Sr. Manager, Supply Chain Optimization & Digitalization Enablement , the Senior Analyst serves as the functional owner of the Inventory Optimization capability across Procurement Operations. The role leads complex optimization and digital enablement initiatives, translates data into actionable business recommendations, and establishes scalable analytical practices that improve inventory, service, cost, operational efficiency, and decision-making. The role combines deep inventory management expertise with advanced analytics, digital enablement, data stewardship, and continuous improvement. The analyst owns and advances inventory optimization methodologies, replenishment strategies, supply chain parameters, supporting technologies, and decision-support capabilities. The analyst also translates the approved Inventory Policy into optimization methodologies, parameters, controls, and recommendations, in partnership with the policy owner and operational teams. Acting as a bridge between Supply Chain and Data, Analytics, AI, and Technology partners, the analyst connects business challenges with practical and scalable solutions that remain operationally relevant, governed, integrated, adopted, and sustainable. Success in this role requires strong supply chain and business acumen, curiosity to understand how operational teams work, and the ability to apply data, analytics, automation, and emerging technologies to deliver measurable business value. Define and monitor inventory performance indicators, connect results to strategic objectives, and proactively identify risks, root causes, and corrective or preventive actions. Translate model outputs and analytical findings into actionable recommendations that balance inventory, DSI, service level, cost, and operational constraints. Present options, trade-offs, business cases, benefits, and risks to influence leadership decisions and investment priorities. Digital Solutions & Analytics Enablement, 25% Lead the design, maintenance, enhancement, and governance of analytical tools, dashboards, optimization models, and decision-support solutions used by Procurement Operations. Develop flexible and scalable capabilities that can adapt to evolving business needs, priorities, and operating models. Drive the modernization of analytical capabilities through automation, standardization, AI-enabled capabilities, and integration with enterprise data platforms. Identify and lead opportunities to streamline workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve decision quality and business outcomes using the most appropriate analytical, automation, AI, and digital technologies. Data Management, Business Intelligence & Governance, 20% Lead complex data extraction, transformation, integration, validation, and troubleshooting activities across operational and enterprise systems, ensuring data reliability and usability. Define and govern datasets, integrations, business rules, data definitions, and documentation supporting supply chain analytics and digital solutions. Promote data stewardship by improving the quality, integrity, accessibility, transparency, and business understanding of supply chain data. Establish and maintain analytical standards, data governance practices, validation methodologies, and reporting frameworks to support consistent decision-making. Coach and review the work of analysts where required, ensuring adherence to data, reporting, and governance standards. Strategic Projects & Continuous Improvement, 25% Lead strategic initiatives involving inventory optimization, business intelligence, analytics modernization, automation, scalable digital transformation, and process improvement. Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to identify opportunities, evaluate root causes and alternative approaches, align priorities, and implement sustainable business solutions. About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
At Anthropic, we're building AI systems that are safe, beneficial, and transformative. Our mission is to develop AI that benefits humanity, and we believe the most powerful capabilities emerge when we thoughtfully bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and real-world applications.
Frontier AI runs on datacenters, and the world is in the middle of the largest infrastructure buildout in a generation. The binding constraint on progress is increasingly everything around the chips: land, power, permits, equipment, and the design and construction of the buildings themselves. Bringing a single site online involves hundreds of people, thousands of components, and decisions that move enormous amounts of capital. Much of that work still runs on spreadsheets and handoffs.
At Anthropic, we're building software and Claude-powered tools to help Anthropic scale out its compute, and we think there's an enormous opportunity to rethink how that work gets done. It's early, it's already having a real impact, and the engineers who join now will shape how one of the most consequential buildouts in the world gets done.
We're looking for strong, versatile software engineers who love building for people doing real work in the physical world. You'll embed with the teams that source sites, design buildings, procure equipment, and manage construction, learn their work deeply, and build the tools and systems they rely on every day. Datacenter experience is a big plus, but what matters most is that you can earn the trust of expert operators, model a messy domain cleanly, and move fast.
Responsibilities

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic's production models undergo sophisticated post-training processes to enhance their capabilities, alignment, and safety. As a Research Engineer on our Post-Training team, you'll train our base models through the complete post-training stack to deliver the production Claude models that users interact with.
You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and production engineering, implementing, scaling, and improving post-training techniques like Constitutional AI, RLHF, and other alignment methodologies. Your work will directly impact the quality, safety, and capabilities of our production models.
Note: For this role, we conduct all interviews in Python. This role may require responding to incidents on short-notice, including on weekends.
Responsibilities:
Implement and optimize post-training techniques at scale on frontier models
Conduct research to develop and optimize post-training recipes that directly improve production model quality
Design, build, and run robust, efficient pipelines for model fine-tuning and evaluation
Develop tools to measure and improve model performance across various dimensions
Collaborate with research teams to translate emerging techniques into production-ready implementations
Debug complex issues in training pipelines and model behavior
Help establish best practices for reliable, reproducible model post-training
You may be a good fit if you:
Thrive in controlled chaos and are energised, rather than overwhelmed, when juggling multiple urgent priorities
Adapt quickly to changing priorities
Maintain clarity when debugging complex, time-sensitive issues
Have strong software engineering skills with experience building complex ML systems
Are comfortable working with large-scale distributed systems and high-performance computing
Have experience with training, fine-tuning, or evaluating large language models
Can balance research exploration with engineering rigor and operational reliability
Are adept at analyzing and debugging model training processes
Enjoy collaborating across research and engineering disciplines
Can navigate ambiguity and make progress in fast-moving research environments
Strong candidates may also:
Have experience with LLMs
Have a keen interest in AI safety and responsible deployment
We welcome candidates at various experience levels, with a preference for senior engineers who have hands-on experience with frontier AI systems. However, proficiency in Python, deep learning frameworks, and distributed computing is required for this role.

We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit
anthropic.com/careers
directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the Role:
Anthropic's ML Performance and Scaling team trains our production pretrained models, work that directly shapes the company's future and our mission to build safe, beneficial AI systems. As a Research Engineer on this team, you'll ensure our frontier models train reliably, efficiently, and at scale. This is demanding, high-impact work that requires both deep technical expertise and a genuine passion for the craft of large-scale ML systems.
This role lives at the boundary between research and engineering. You'll work across our entire production training stack: performance optimization, hardware debugging, experimental design, and launch coordination. During launches, the team works in tight lockstep, responding to production issues that can't wait for tomorrow.
Responsibilities:
Own critical aspects of our production pretraining pipeline, including model operations, performance optimization, observability, and reliability
Debug and resolve complex issues across the full stack—from hardware errors and networking to training dynamics and evaluation infrastructure
Design and run experiments to improve training efficiency, reduce step time, increase uptime, and enhance model performance
Respond to on-call incidents during model launches, diagnosing problems quickly and coordinating solutions across teams
Build and maintain production logging, monitoring dashboards, and evaluation infrastructure
Add new capabilities to the training codebase, such as long context support or novel architectures
Collaborate closely with teammates across SF and London, as well as with Tokens, Architectures, and Systems teams
Contribute to the team's institutional knowledge by documenting systems, debugging approaches, and lessons learned
You May Be a Good Fit If You:
Have hands-on experience training large language models, or deep expertise with JAX, TPU, PyTorch, or large-scale distributed systems
Genuinely enjoy both research and engineering work—you'd describe your ideal split as roughly 50/50 rather than heavily weighted toward one or the other
Are excited about being on-call for production systems, working long days during launches, and solving hard problems under pressure
Thrive when working on whatever is most impactful, even if that changes day-to-day based on what the production model needs
Excel at debugging complex, ambiguous problems across multiple layers of the stack
Communicate clearly and collaborate effectively, especially when coordinating across time zones or during high-stress incidents
Are passionate about the work itself and want to refine your craft as a research engineer
Care about the societal impacts of AI and responsible scaling
Strong Candidates May Also Have:
Previous experience training LLM’s or working extensively with JAX/TPU, PyTorch, or other ML frameworks at scale
Contributed to open-source LLM frameworks (e.g., open_lm, llm-foundry, mesh-transformer-jax)
Published research on model training, scaling laws, or ML systems
Experience with production ML systems, observability tools, or evaluation infrastructure
Background as a systems engineer, quant, or in other roles requiring both technical depth and operational excellence
What Makes This Role Unique:
This is not a typical research engineering role. The work is highly operational—you'll be deeply involved in keeping our production models training smoothly, which means being responsive to incidents, flexible about priorities, and comfortable with uncertainty. During launches, the team often works extended hours and may need to respond to issues on evenings and weekends.
However, this operational intensity comes with extraordinary learning opportunities. You'll gain hands-on experience with some of the largest, most sophisticated training runs in the industry. You'll work alongside world-class researchers and engineers, and the institutional knowledge you build will compound in ways that can't be easily transferred. For people who thrive on this type of work, it's uniquely rewarding.
We're building a close-knit team of people who genuinely care about doing excellent work together. If you're someone who wants to be part of training the models that will define the future of AI—and you're excited about the full reality of what that entails—we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.description: Amazon AIR is building one of the most ambitious dedicated air transportation networks in the world, designed to redefine delivery speed and selection for hundreds of millions of customers. As we scale this network, we need leaders who can tackle complex operational challenges and deliver results that customers feel every single day. We are seeking a Flight Capacity Planner to join the Flight Scheduling team and help shape the future of Amazon AIR. In this role, you will own the development and optimization of flight capacity strategies across long, medium and short term planning horizons, including flight schedule design, capacity allocation, and network modeling. You will also lead high impact, cross functional initiatives that drive efficiency, reduce cost, and improve service performance across the air network. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution. You will partner with leaders across Amazon AIR, including Operations, Finance, and Analytics, and directly influence senior leadership decisions that shape how millions of packages move through our network. Your recommendations will balance customer experience with cost effectiveness, and your work will have a measurable impact on Amazon's end to end transportation ecosystem. If you thrive on solving complex, ambiguous problems at scale, want to innovate across air and ground transportation solutions, and are passionate about delighting customers, we'd love for you to help us make Amazon AIR history. Key job responsibilities - Lead flight schedule development across multiple time horizons within Amazon AIR, serving as the primary point of contact for cross functional business units including ground transportation, fulfillment centers, and last mile operations. - Develop and present data driven recommendations to senior leadership on network design changes, route adjustments, and capacity investments. - Develop and optimize capacity plans and network strategy, driving continuous improvement across customer experience, cost efficiency, and sustainability metrics. - Evaluate complex tradeoffs between customer needs and cost, building consensus across partner teams such as Finance, Operations, Process Engineering, and Procurement to drive aligned decision making. - Partner with Research Science and Technology as a subject matter expert to design and develop next generation planning and forecasting tools. - Analyze flight utilization, block hour efficiency, and network performance data to identify optimization opportunities - Monitor and manage flight capacity allocation across the network, ensuring alignment between demand forecasts, and operational constraints. - Navigate ambiguity while managing and coordinating multiple concurrent projects in a fast paced, deadline driven environment, taking full ownership and accountability for processes and delivering on commitments. - Domestic travel up to 10% of the time. A day in the life As a Flight Capacity Planner, you will develop and optimize flight schedule operating plans, identify new opportunities, and communicate those plans across internal teams. You will also contribute to long term strategic recommendations for fleet deployment, gateway utilization, hub operations, and sortation capacity needs. Your day will blend data analysis, network modeling, and cross functional collaboration. You will build flight schedules to accommodate peak volume, analyze network to identify under-performing routes, or present capacity tradeoff scenarios to senior leadership. You will regularly partner with AIR carriers, operations, ground transportation teams to ensure flight schedules are tightly integrated with the broader network. This role is ideal for someone who is energized by solving complex network optimization problems that directly impact millions of customer deliveries. About the team Flight Scheduling is one of the pillars of the Planning & Performance (P&P) organization within AIR Supply Chain and Analytics (SC&A). Flight Scheduling owns the creation and revision of short to long term operational plans, developing flight schedules from several months out through just days before departure. The team is responsible for setting the course for Amazon AIR to continuously raise the bar for customers by delivering the best possible mix of fast delivery speeds, low costs, and superior quality and reliability across the network.

회사 소개
쿠팡은 고객 감동 실현을 위해 존재합니다. 고객들이 "쿠팡 없이 그동안 어떻게 살았을까?" 라고 말할 때, 비로소 우리의 미션을 실현하고 있음을 알 수 있습니다. 고객들의 쇼핑과 식사, 생활 전반을 편하게 만들겠다는 유일한 집념으로 쿠팡은 수억 달러 규모의 이커머스 산업 전반의 혁신을 이끌고 있습니다. 쿠팡은 가장 빠르게 성장하는 이커머스 기업 중 하나로, 국내 커머스 업계에서의 독보적인 입지와, 고객 신뢰를 구축했습니다.

jobs.description: Summary: This role builds and supports the data models, dashboards, pipelines, and reports the Technology Financial Operations Office uses to manage technology cost, Cloud FinOps, TCO, portfolio, demand, and productivity information. The work is to move recurring reporting off manual spreadsheets and one-off files and onto governed analytics products with reliable refreshes, consistent definitions, and clear ownership. Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric are the corporate platforms for this work; strong comparable enterprise BI experience will also be considered. The test of success is whether leadership uses the reporting as delivered, without rebuilding it in a spreadsheet first and without the numbers falling apart when someone checks them. Who We Are Looking For The Technology Financial Operations Office is looking for a hands-on Data Analytics & BI Engineer to be based in Dublin. The broader team is distributed, with several senior stakeholders and complementary roles based in other offices, so this role will need to partner effectively across locations. This is a build-and-support role: the successful candidate does the BI engineering and data modeling directly, works with the stakeholders who use the output, and stays with those products once they are in production. The work runs the full path from a loosely defined reporting request through discovery, data preparation, modeling, build, validation, release, and ongoing support. It suits someone comfortable with both technical partners and non-technical business users, who can explain what a number means as readily as they can build the model behind it. The role is judged on what reaches production and gets used, not on the volume of reports produced. Why This Role Is Important to Us The Technology Financial Operations Office is moving recurring reporting off manually maintained spreadsheets and one-off files and onto BI products that can be reused across functions. Source data is fragmented across finance, cloud, procurement, portfolio, and service management systems, and the questions leadership asks keep changing as the cost agenda matures. This role makes the answers reliable enough to act on without side calculations or manual reconciliation. Near-term work includes reporting for IT Total Cost of Ownership and showback, Cloud FinOps spend and optimization tracking, productivity and demand reporting, and the retirement of high-effort manual reports. These are starting points rather than the boundary of the role; the same discipline will be applied to further cost and financial analytics products as the Business Office defines them. What You Will Be Responsible For Build and maintain data pipelines, transformations, semantic models, dashboards, and refreshable reporting solutions using Microsoft Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, and related analytics tools. Modernize spreadsheet-based reporting by converting recurring, manually maintained reports into governed, reusable BI products with defined owners and a support model. Develop reporting that supports technology financial management, IT Total Cost of Ownership, Cloud FinOps, portfolio, demand, and headcount processes, including showback views and optimization tracking. Prepare, reconcile, and model data from finance, cloud, procurement, portfolio, headcount, and service management systems, including the transformation logic and refresh processes that keep those sources aligned. Build reusable datasets, semantic models, and measures, together with the validation checks and exception reporting that surface data quality issues before they reach a report. Design dashboards and reports that Business Office teams, finance partners, and senior technology leaders can read and act on without a walkthrough. Work directly with business stakeholders to capture requirements, agree definitions, and validate results, translating loosely defined questions into something the available data can answer. Apply controlled release, change, and access practices so reporting stays secure, traceable, and safe to change once it is in production. Document sources, definitions, assumptions, calculation logic, refresh schedules, and known limitations. Support delivered products after launch, including issue intake, triage, resolution, and continuous improvement. What We Value The following skills and qualities matter most in this role: Ownership of a vague reporting request from discovery through build, validation, release, and ongoing support, including the unglamorous parts, without needing to be chased. Comfort working with imperfect source data, and the discipline to reconcile differences, document assumptions, and state plainly what the data will and will not support. A clear line between actuals, forecasts, estimates, and advisory analysis, held consistently and without turning every number into a caveat. The ability to explain a number, its limitations, and the tradeoffs behind it to a finance partner, a technical peer, or a senior executive. Comfort working across functions where definitions, source data, and ownership are still maturing, and the patience to build alignment rather than wait for it. A product mindset that treats reporting as a supported capability with an owner, a backlog, and a roadmap rather than a series of one-off builds. Exacting standards for documentation, data quality, governance, and auditability, because these reports are relied on every month and are expected to hold up to review. Education & Preferred Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Finance, Business Analytics, Engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered. Hands-on experience building BI solutions using Microsoft Power BI and Microsoft Fabric preferred, including Power Query, DAX, semantic models, dashboards, dataflows, lakehouse or warehouse patterns, and SQL; strong comparable enterprise BI experience will also be considered. Demonstrated experience building data models, measures, reconciliations, and refresh processes that span multiple source systems and survive routine change in those sources. Familiarity with financial, portfolio, procurement, cloud, and headcount data, and with IT cost transparency concepts such as Total Cost of Ownership, showback, and Cloud FinOps, preferred. Experience documenting data lineage, definitions, calculations, and controls in a governed or regulated enterprise environment preferred. Experience working directly with non-technical stakeholders to capture requirements, agree definitions, and validate results before release preferred. Additional Requirements This is a matrixed role. The work spans finance, FinOps, portfolio, procurement, and technology teams, with requirements that shift as the cost agenda matures and source data that rarely arrives clean. Comfort operating with that level of ambiguity, and the persistence to resolve it rather than route around it, matters as much as technical skill. Work Requirements Full-time role based in Dublin, Ireland. Expected to follow applicable State Street office attendance requirements for the role and location. Standard business hours, with flexibility as needed to support stakeholders across time zones; limited travel may be required.
